# NIPAT 0.7.1 research distribution evidence

## Decision

Maintainer Gregorio Dalia requested publication for domain evaluation by the researchers. Codex performed the technical review on his behalf, with independent review of the code and evidence. The decision covered pre-1.0 research use. It did not attest clinical validity or all desktop scenarios; previously published versions retained their identities.

## Reported Windows observation

The maintainer installed 0.7.0a1, commit `1b601081a4aff9efe1806c921fd7ac963feea7b7`, on Windows 11 with WSL2. This record draws on his supplied logs and tables, without direct access to his computer.

The automatic DNPcall → Contamination workflow used one BAM. Both stages and the workflow returned `succeeded`, with exit code zero. Counts and genotypes for all 11 DNP sites matched previous separate runs. Contamination retained 10 sites, with zero per-site estimates, mean and standard deviation. This demonstrated chaining and numerical agreement for the tested case. It did not biologically establish absence of contamination or validate CPI, other inputs or all parameters. Personal paths, coordinates and sample names are omitted. The 0.6 self-tests belong to their own installation.

## Candidate source and tests

The candidate was `9bbdb8bf1163302c77ce94be687596b07e9d1250`. [Full CI](https://github.com/GregorioDalia/nipat-desktop/actions/runs/40331065857) passed Windows and Linux checks, real R/samtools regressions and the required final gate. Local checks comprised 683 application tests (681 passed and two platform exclusions), 138 CI/publication checks and links across 36 Markdown documents. A real POSIX terminal session exercised resizing, arrow keys, W selection, text fallback and recovery, submenu cancellation and Ctrl+C. It was not a manual test of the Windows console in the new EXE.

All five jobs in [installer build 40331221644](https://github.com/GregorioDalia/nipat-desktop/actions/runs/40331221644) passed, including the joint `installer-required` gate. The downloaded combined report agreed with the per-package evidence. The release JSON binds both installers, the manifest and the shared scientific archive.

Package evidence was downloaded and reviewed independently from source. All 9 Windows checks, 12 installed Ubuntu package checks and 7 dependency checks were true.

The Windows check staged portable Python 3.12.10 in a path with spaces and non-ASCII characters. It verified imports, catalog, menu, three cancellations to the main menu and five `--dry-run` plans, with original inputs preserved. It did not execute Inno Setup, WSL or R, or establish interactive Windows console navigation.

The Ubuntu runner installed the DEB and ran all four analyses and a five-stage workflow as a non-root user. The workflow covered DNPcall, Contamination, CPI and two independent SNPcall stages. Nine runs succeeded. Verification included numerical outputs, identities, inputs, intermediates, logs, reinstallation, removal and retention of data and preferences. A separate dependency check started with an Ubuntu container lacking Python, Docker and Compose; it neither started the runtime nor granted the user Docker access. Neither trial was interactive Ubuntu Desktop testing.

Scientific regressions inside the image included an independent informative CPI case with expected fetal fraction 8% and log10 CPI 0.903, agreement between separate and compound analyses, and failure handling.

## Comparison against the observed Windows source

The operational inventory identified 181 identical and 18 modified files. R sources, the in-image engine and orchestration, runtime definitions and `compose.yaml` were identical. Reviewed differences covered version, Windows manifest validation, input guidance, menus and cancellation, run cleanup and their tests.

`v0.7.1.json` lists the before/after SHA-256 of each changed file. The publisher recalculated the comparison from both commits and retained it in `baseline-source-check.json`. Documentation and `.github` procedures were reviewed separately from the deployed operational inventory. This comparison made no claim that installer binaries matched or that the candidate EXE had been manually installed.

## Outstanding desktop and domain work

Windows checks still needed clean WSL activation, coexistence with existing installations and the complete reinstall/removal matrix. Interactive Ubuntu Desktop checks still needed clean installation, pre-existing Docker, reinstall and removal. The researchers' 0.7.1 campaign concerned representative inputs, multiple samples and known pair roles, parameter choices, interpretation and Windows console interaction. Device-protection blocks were to be recorded. The installer had no NIPAT Authenticode signature.
